doc.title: Von Freeman — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Chicago repertoire, bands and the end of the big-band era
title: King Kolax recruits Gene Ammons; Freeman stays in school
summary: Kolax came to DuSable for the two tenor hotshots; Jug left, and Freeman stayed to finish school.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: What about [King] Kolax? All that came in later?
No. Kolax come along about the same time as Earl Hines, because when Earl Hines left the Grand Terrace, Kolax went in with his big band.
So you’re talking about early ’40s to mid-’40s.
This is like ’39, ’40, ’41. When Kolax came by the school to get the two little hotshots, which was Gene Ammons and myself, on tenor . . .
Yeah. Jug went on the road with him, and Jug never came back, because Jug went with Kolax, and then he went with Billy Eckstine.
